1. (Currently Amended) A hydraulic energy retention system, the system comprising:a body with a piston separating a hydraulic fluid from a pressurized gas;
a discharge port in fluid communication with the hydraulic fluid; and
a stop operable to an engaged position to block movement of the piston past the stop and toward the discharge port;
wherein the stop, in the engaged position, allows the piston to move away from the discharge port.
2. (Original) The system of claim 1, wherein the stop comprises a pin positioned between the piston and the discharge port, wherein the pin extends into a path of the of the piston when in the engaged position.
3. (Canceled)
4. (Original) The system of claim 1, wherein the stop comprises:a pin having a portion located exterior of the body; and
an actuator movable into the engaged position where the actuator pushes the pin inside of the body between the piston and the discharge port.
5. (Original) The system of claim 1, further comprising a bootstrap reservoir having a low- pressure outlet and a high-pressure input, wherein the discharge port is in communication with the low-pressure outlet.
6. (Original) The system of claim 5, wherein the stop, in the engaged position, allows the piston to move away from the discharge port.
7. (Original) The system of claim 5, wherein the stop comprises:a pin having a portion located exterior of the body; and
an actuator movable into the engaged position where the actuator pushes the pin inside of the body between the piston and the discharge port.
8. (Original) An aircraft hydraulic system, the system comprising:a hydraulic circuit comprising a system pressure circuit and a return circuit;
a pump having a pump outlet connected to the system pressure circuit and a pump inlet connected to the return circuit;
a hydraulic accumulator comprising a piston separating a hydraulic fluid from a pressurized gas and a discharge port in communication with the hydraulic fluid and the return circuit; and
a stop operable to an engaged position to block movement of the piston past the stop and toward the discharge port.
9. (Original) The system of claim 8, wherein the stop, in the engaged position, allows the piston to move away from the discharge port.
10. (Original) The system of claim 8, wherein the stop comprises a pin positioned between the piston and the discharge port, wherein the pin extends into a path of the of the piston when in the engaged position.
11. (Original) The system of claim 8, wherein the stop comprises:a pin having a portion located exterior of the hydraulic accumulator; and
an actuator movable into the engaged position where the actuator pushes the pin inside of the hydraulic accumulator between the piston and the discharge port.
12. (Original) The system of claim 11, wherein the stop, in the engaged position, allows the piston to move away from the discharge port.
13. (Original) The system of claim 8, further comprising a bootstrap reservoir having a low- pressure outlet connected to the return circuit and a high-pressure input connected to the system pressure circuit, wherein the discharge port is connected to the bootstrap reservoir.
14. (Original) The system of claim 13, wherein the stop, in the engaged position, allows the piston to move away from the discharge port.
15. (Original) The system of claim 13, wherein the stop comprises a pin positioned between the piston and the discharge port, wherein the pin extends into a path of the of the piston when in the engaged position.
16. (Original) The system of claim 13, wherein the stop comprises:a pin having a portion located exterior of the hydraulic accumulator; and
an actuator movable into the engaged position where the actuator pushes the pin inside of the hydraulic accumulator between the piston and the discharge port.
17. (Original) A method of retaining hydraulic energy in an aircraft's hydraulic system, comprising:using the hydraulic system comprising a hydraulic circuit having a system pressure circuit and a return circuit, a pump having a pump outlet connected to the system pressure circuit and a pump inlet connected to the return circuit, and a hydraulic accumulator comprising a piston separating a pressurized hydraulic fluid from a pressurized gas and a discharge port communicating the hydraulic fluid to the return circuit;
running the pump thereby pressurizing the hydraulic circuit;
turning off the pump;
operating a stop, with the pump off, to an engaged position stopping movement of the piston past the stop and toward the discharge port thereby retaining the hydraulic fluid at the pump inlet at a selected pump inlet pressure; and
restarting the pump comprising operating the stop to a disengaged position allowing movement of the piston toward the discharge port and then starting the pump.
18. (Original) The method of claim 17, wherein the stop, in the engaged position, allows the piston to move away from the discharge port.
19. (Original) The method of claim 17, wherein the hydraulic system further comprises a bootstrap reservoir having a low-pressure outlet connected to the return circuit and a high- pressure input connected to the system pressure circuit, wherein the discharge port is connected to the bootstrap reservoir.
20. (Original) The method of claim 19, wherein the stop comprises:a pin having a portion located exterior of the hydraulic accumulator; and
an actuator movable into the engaged position where the actuator pushes the pin inside of the hydraulic accumulator between the piston and the discharge port.
